habitat: Fairly dry open woodland with bare or stony ground, including shrubby Acacia, mopane and mixed broad-leaved woodland, and bushwillow along drainage lines.
summary: A nomadic lowveld lark that appears in numbers, breeds, and moves on. Adults are compact, with a small bill, a plain face, an indistinct eyebrow that stops short of the bill, streaked upperparts, a rufous wing panel, a white throat, a lightly streaked buff chest and a pale belly. The sexes are not described as differing in plumage. Males sing from bushes and in display flight. A total length, and juvenile or chick colours, are not given in the texts used here.

similar.note: Sabota Lark has a white eyebrow that reaches the bill area and no rufous wing panel. Monotonous Lark’s white throat is obvious when it sings.
Rufous-naped Lark is larger, crested, and whistles from an open perch. Monotonous Lark has a plain face and a rufous wing panel.

head.pattern: plain face; the white eyebrow stops short of the bill and is indistinct

underparts.pattern: lightly streaked buff chest between the white throat and the pale belly

wings.pattern: distinct rufous panel on the wing

viewNotes.note: Streaked upperparts and a rufous wing panel. Males use bushes for display flights. The tail pattern is not described beyond an old alternative name, white-tailed lark, which the texts used here do not explain.
A white throat, conspicuous when the bird is singing, and a lightly streaked buff chest.
Streaked upperparts. The rump is not given a separate colour.
Small bill, plain face, rufous wing panel and white throat in one profile.

calls.description: The male’s song is the field mark when the bird is otherwise hard to identify; the texts used here call it distinctive and do not transcribe the notes. A female song is not described.

research.note: Kemp classed it as a visiting breeder. SABAP1 calls the movements nomadic and not fully understood, and says it is sometimes treated as an intra-African migrant. Months are October–June, covering Roberts egg-laying from October to March and atlas breeding records from January to June. July–September are not listed. The song syllables are not transcribed in these texts. The grade A recording is from Polokwane; a grade B song from Kruger was not preferred. Chick plumage and a total length were not found. The iNaturalist account name is tjeerd.
